content.comment_body: We are using [product_name] without display, hardware version [version_no] ([article_no]) with firmware version [version_no], alongside the [product_name] display ([article_no]) with firmware version [version_no]. We configured Function Blocks for message text switching by using the M27 bit to indicate message differences. Up until [version_no], all worked well — messages were acknowledged without issues regardless of M27 being ON or OFF. However, after updating to [product_name] [version_no] ([article_no]) with firmware version [version_no], we can no longer acknowledge alarms on the display when the M27 bit is ON, while it still works when M27 is OFF. In simulation, both functions acknowledge as expected, but after downloading to hardware, the error appears. All BM settings are enabled on both the display and PLC hardware. We've attached the program showing the error. Input 1 toggles the M27 bit, and Input 2 enables the message.
Topic closed due to duplicate posting. The active discussion is available at: [url] Kind regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: The user migrated from [product_name] hardware and firmware version [version_no] to [version_no], and encountered a new issue: message acknowledgment on the display, triggered by the M27 bit in the ON state, no longer works as it did previously. In simulation, the process works, but this error only occurs on actual hardware. This indicates a firmware compatibility or regression issue that affects real-use scenarios.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects message acknowledgment functionality to remain consistent with previous hardware and simulation, regardless of the M27 bit state. They also expect new hardware and firmware versions to maintain existing workflows and not introduce operational issues.
